meta.theme: the cycle of imitation and flight assumes a mark that can be bought exactly; a mark whose price is accumulated cannot be completed by a copier, so it is never abandoned, the test moves from possession to manner, and its holders can deny sincerely that any marking occurs

meta.reviewer_notes: A scene followed by five paragraphs of reflection, with the crucial work done by the fifth and sixth: the fifth says such marks look like nothing but taste from the inside, and the sixth refuses to call the connoisseur a hypocrite. Readers who want a denunciation supply one, which is what four of the five questions are built to catch.

quality.adversarial_review: The live rival throughout is the denunciation the passage declines to make. Q1's is the option that connoisseurs use their knowledge deliberately to keep others at a distance, which the sixth paragraph refuses by calling the pleasure real and denying that anything must be performed. Q2's unsupported statement is about resentment between quick and slow learners, a thoroughly plausible claim that appears nowhere, while the other three can each be pointed at in the third, fourth and fifth paragraphs. Q3's rival is the option that a copy can always be told from the original, which the third paragraph denies of bought marks in so many words. Q4's rival is the option ranking one kind of mark above the other in value to its owner, a comparison the passage never makes, since it compares durability and visibility only. Q5's rival is the reading of the scene as a counter-example, whereas the fourth paragraph uses the rug as its own illustration and the scene supplies the mechanism the reflection then names.

passage.title: Not Quite the One You Wanted

paragraphs.text: At dinner a guest admired the rug under the table, and said, pleasantly, that he had been looking for one like it for two years. His host said that this was very kind of him, and then, after the smallest possible pause, that it was not quite what the guest supposed: the pattern belonged to a different valley, the older workshops there had closed within a decade of the war, and the pieces sold under that name now were almost all later copies, perfectly good in themselves. The conversation moved on inside the same sentence. Nobody was embarrassed, and nothing was scored. What had been established, gently and beyond appeal, was that the guest could buy the rug and would still not have the thing.

The familiar account of how status marks itself would make this a moment in a cycle. A group at the top takes something up; those below acquire it; the mark, having lost its power to distinguish, is dropped from above and replaced; and the whole apparatus moves on a notch, leaving the copiers holding last season's proof of arrival. The cycle explains a great deal that would otherwise look like mere restlessness: the migration of holiday destinations, the rise and fall of forenames, the steady abandonment of any word that becomes widely used for something respectable.

Notice, though, what that account has to assume. It assumes that the mark can be had by anybody prepared to pay for it, and that once it has been had it is the same mark. Of objects, and of everything sold beside them, this is true. A coat is a coat; the copy is not detectably a copy; the person at the top has no defence except to move, because possession is the whole of the test and possession has been achieved. Where the price is money, flight is the only strategy there is.

A second kind of mark costs something that cannot be handed over. It is accumulated: hours, attention, the slow correction of error, and above all the company of people who already have it and will say so when one is wrong. A mark of this kind is not an object but a relation to objects, and a relation cannot be delivered in a box. The copy is always detectably a copy, not because the copier is stupid but because what he is copying is a history he does not have. Indeed his arrival is what creates the occasion, since nobody is corrected about a rug he has never mentioned. And here the cycle does not begin at all. Nothing has to be abandoned, because nothing has been successfully taken. The rug stays. What moves is where the test is applied: from whether you have one to what you are able to say about it.

Marks of this kind are accordingly far more durable than the ones the cycle describes, and far less visible. They cannot be taxed. They cannot be undercut by a competitor in a shop, or made available more cheaply by anybody at all. They leave no receipts. And they present themselves, to those who hold them, as nothing more than taste, which is the strongest position a mark can occupy: its holders are able to deny that any marking is going on, and to mean it, because from the inside there is nothing to see except a preference that happens to be well informed.

The account should not be pressed into saying more than it can carry. It does not make the connoisseur a hypocrite; the pleasure he takes in the difference between the two valleys is real, and nothing in the argument requires it to be performed. Nor does it hold that money has stopped working, which it plainly has not. The claim is narrower and stranger than either. A mark whose price is accumulated need not be surrendered when it spreads downward, for the simple reason that it does not spread; and a mark that cannot be copied has no use for the flight that everybody takes status to consist of.

questions.target_mistake: reading the passage as an exposure of connoisseurs when its last paragraph declines to call them insincere
questions.prediction_target: The learner should be able to say: some marks cannot be copied because their price is accumulated rather than paid, so the cycle of imitation and flight never starts for them.
questions.stem: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?

options.A: A mark whose price is accumulated rather than paid is not abandoned, because it cannot be copied.
options.B: Every mark of status is eventually given up by the people who first took it up.
options.C: Those who possess such knowledge deploy it deliberately in order to keep other people at a distance.
options.D: The exchange at dinner shows how a compliment can be converted into a correction.

explanation.expert_notice: The final paragraph states the claim in its narrowest form, and it is the only place in the passage where the author says what he is and is not asserting. A mark whose price is accumulated need not be surrendered when it spreads downward, because it does not spread, and such a mark has no use for flight.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option is that sentence compressed, and it keeps the causal order the passage insists on. The mark is not abandoned, and the reason is that the copying never succeeds, which the fourth paragraph establishes by making the mark a relation rather than an object. Everything else in the passage supports that claim: the scene shows the failed copy, the third paragraph shows why bought marks behave differently, and the fifth draws out the consequences.
explanation.question_type_note: In a passage that opens with a scene, the main idea is never the scene. Look instead for the paragraph in which the author narrows his own claim, since that is where he tells you what he has been arguing.
explanation.reading_habit: When a passage ends by saying what its claim is not, read that paragraph twice. It contains both the thesis and the boundary, and options are built out of the territory just outside the boundary.

distractors.why_wrong: This is the familiar account set out in the second paragraph, and the rest of the passage exists to find the case it does not fit. The fourth paragraph says of that case that the cycle does not begin at all.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the received wisdom about status, it is stated early and at length, and the passage credits it with explaining a great deal.

distractors.why_wrong: The last paragraph refuses it in a sentence of its own: the connoisseur is not a hypocrite, the pleasure is real, and nothing in the argument requires it to be performed. Deliberate deployment is exactly what the author declines to claim.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the live rival, because the opening scene reads like a manoeuvre and the fifth paragraph calls the position the strongest a mark can occupy, which sounds like strategy.

distractors.why_wrong: The dinner occupies the first of six paragraphs and is there to supply a case. What the passage argues about is why the guest's purchase would not have helped him, which is a claim about kinds of mark rather than about conversational technique.
distractors.seductive_element: The scene is the most memorable thing in the passage and is described in more detail than any of the arguments that follow it.

questions.target_mistake: accepting a claim about how people feel towards one another, which the passage never discusses, because it fits the social situation being described
questions.stem: Which of the following CANNOT be inferred from the passage?

options.A: A mark that can be bought exactly is likely to be given up by those who took it up first.
options.B: The test applied to the second kind of mark is not whether a person owns the object.
options.C: A person who acquires such knowledge quickly is resented by those who acquired it slowly.
options.D: Someone may hold a mark of the second kind without taking himself to be marking anything.

explanation.expert_notice: Three of these can be pointed at. The third paragraph has the person at the top with no defence except to move; the fourth moves the test from whether you have one to what you can say about it; the fifth has holders denying that any marking is going on and meaning it. The fourth statement has no sentence behind it.
explanation.correct_reasoning: Nothing in the passage concerns what anybody feels about anybody else. The argument is about what can and cannot be transferred, and it treats the correction at dinner as gentle and unscored rather than as resentful. A claim about resentment would need a sentence about the attitudes of holders towards newcomers, and the only sentence touching their attitudes says the opposite, that they see nothing but a well-informed preference.
explanation.question_type_note: A cannot-be-inferred question is three location tasks and one failure to locate. Work by pointing rather than by judging plausibility, since the answer is usually the most believable statement in the set.
explanation.reading_habit: For each option, name the sentence that supports it before deciding. If you find yourself arguing that something must be true of people in that situation, you have found the answer.

distractors.why_wrong: The second and third paragraphs together give this: the mark is dropped from above once it has lost its power to distinguish, and where the price is money flight is the only strategy there is.
distractors.seductive_element: The claim is assembled from two paragraphs rather than stated in one, so a reader hunting for a single sentence does not find it.

distractors.why_wrong: The fourth paragraph states exactly this as its closing move, saying that what shifts is where the test is applied, from whether you have one to what you are able to say about it.
distractors.seductive_element: The passage puts the point through the rug and in the first person of the test, so the option's flat general phrasing looks like an addition rather than a paraphrase.

distractors.why_wrong: The fifth paragraph ends on this, saying holders can deny that any marking is going on and mean it, since from the inside there is only a well-informed preference. The sixth then declines to call them hypocrites.
distractors.seductive_element: It sits in the clause readers treat as an aside about how things feel, and remarks about feeling are the ones most often dismissed as not stated.

questions.target_mistake: attributing to the cycle the very feature the passage says it lacks, namely a copy that can be told from the original
questions.stem: According to the passage, the cycle of imitation and flight rests on the assumption that

options.A: the mark can be had by anybody who is prepared to pay for it
options.B: those who copy a mark do so in order to be taken for its owners
options.C: a copy can always be told apart from the thing that it copies
options.D: each new mark costs more than the one it has replaced

explanation.expert_notice: The third paragraph exists to name the assumption and does so in its second sentence, in two parts: the mark can be had by anybody prepared to pay for it, and once it has been had it is the same mark. The paragraph then shows what follows, which is that flight is the only available strategy.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option is the first half of that sentence. It is the assumption that makes the rest of the cycle work, since a mark that can be bought will be bought, at which point possession no longer distinguishes anybody and the only move left is to move. The passage's whole argument consists of finding a case where this assumption fails.
explanation.question_type_note: When a passage says notice what the account has to assume, the sentence immediately after is the answer to any question about that assumption. The options will be drawn from the consequences instead.
explanation.reading_habit: Mark the sentence that follows an author's invitation to notice something. Authors use that construction exactly once per argument and they put the load-bearing claim directly after it.

distractors.why_wrong: The motives of copiers are never discussed. The passage describes what happens once a mark has been acquired and says nothing about why anybody wanted it, which is a separate question it does not need.
distractors.seductive_element: Wanting to be taken for someone else is the obvious reason to copy a mark, so the reader supplies a motive the passage left out.

distractors.why_wrong: The third paragraph states the reverse of this for bought marks, saying that a coat is a coat and the copy is not detectably a copy. The detectable copy belongs to the second kind of mark, where the cycle does not operate.
distractors.seductive_element: Detectability is the passage's central idea and appears prominently in the fourth paragraph, so a reader attaches it to the wrong kind of mark.

distractors.why_wrong: No comparison of prices between successive marks appears anywhere. The cycle in the second paragraph turns on a mark losing its power to distinguish, not on the next one costing more.
distractors.seductive_element: Escalating cost is the usual folk account of how status competition works, and the second paragraph's list of migrating fashions invites it.

questions.target_mistake: ranking the two kinds of mark by their worth to the owner, a comparison the passage makes only on durability and visibility
questions.prediction_target: The learner should predict that, since the copier's arrival creates the occasion for correction, acquiring the object brings an outsider into the place where the other test is applied.
questions.stem: Which of the following can most reasonably be inferred from the passage?

options.A: A mark that costs money is worth less to its owner than one whose price is accumulated.
options.B: Connoisseurship is a defence that is taken up deliberately once imitation has started.
options.C: A mark of the second kind will in the end be abandoned in the way the cycle describes.
options.D: Buying the object may make the distance between an outsider and an owner easier to display.

explanation.expert_notice: Two sentences in the fourth paragraph do this work together. The copy is always detectably a copy, and the copier's arrival is what creates the occasion, since nobody is corrected about a rug he has never mentioned. The opening scene is that pair of sentences acted out.
explanation.correct_reasoning: Acquiring the object does not close the gap; it brings the outsider into the conversation where the gap is tested. The guest's two years of looking is precisely what produces the correction, and the correction is what makes the difference between the two men visible to everybody at the table. So the purchase, far from removing the mark, supplies the occasion on which it is shown.
explanation.question_type_note: An inference question at this level joins a general claim to the scene that exemplifies it. Where a passage opens with an incident, check whether an option is the incident's own logic stated in general terms.
explanation.reading_habit: When an author says that something creates the occasion for something else, work out who is better off afterwards. That sentence is usually the hinge of the strongest inference available.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage compares the two kinds of mark on durability, visibility and whether they can be copied, and never on what either is worth to the person holding it. Worth to the owner is a scale the passage does not use.
distractors.seductive_element: The fifth paragraph is a list of advantages, and a reader converts a list of advantages into a judgement of value.

distractors.why_wrong: The sixth paragraph denies that anything is being performed and calls the connoisseur's pleasure real. A defence adopted in response to imitation would be a strategy, which is what the author is at pains not to allege.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the live rival, because the fourth paragraph really does describe the mark holding up under imitation, and holding up under attack sounds like defending.

distractors.why_wrong: The fourth and sixth paragraphs both say the reverse: the cycle does not begin at all, nothing has to be abandoned because nothing has been successfully taken, and such a mark has no use for flight.
distractors.seductive_element: The cycle is presented in the second paragraph as a general law of status, and general laws are expected to catch up with every exception eventually.

questions.target_mistake: treating the opening scene as a problem the argument must accommodate rather than as the case the argument goes on to explain
questions.prediction_target: The learner should be able to say: the scene is one instance, and the paragraphs after it name the mechanism that instance depends on.
questions.stem: The relationship between the exchange at dinner and the paragraphs that follow it is best described as

options.A: an illustration whose details the later argument goes on to call into question
options.B: a counter-example that the argument has to find some way of working around
options.C: a single case of the mechanism the argument afterwards names and explains
options.D: a general claim that the paragraphs following it proceed to narrow down

explanation.expert_notice: The rug reappears twice after the scene, both times as the argument's own example: the rug stays where a bought mark would have to be replaced, and the two valleys return in the last paragraph as the object of the connoisseur's real pleasure. An incident an argument keeps reusing is its case, not its problem.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The scene shows a purchase that would not close a gap, and the fourth paragraph explains why by making the mark a relation rather than an object. Nothing in the scene is corrected, questioned or worked around; it is restated in general terms and then accounted for. That is what it is for a narrative opening to be an instance of a mechanism.
explanation.question_type_note: A relationship question asks how two parts of a passage stand to each other. Check whether the later material explains the earlier, questions it, or is limited by it, since those three answers look alike in summary.
explanation.reading_habit: Track whether an opening scene is picked up again. A scene the argument returns to is being explained; one the argument never mentions again was probably only an attention-getter.

distractors.why_wrong: No detail of the exchange is doubted anywhere. The host's correction is treated as accurate throughout, and the last paragraph takes his interest in the difference between the valleys to be genuine.
distractors.seductive_element: The passage does complicate the reader's first impression of the scene, and complicating an impression feels like questioning the scene.

distractors.why_wrong: The scene is what the argument is built to explain rather than an awkwardness it must survive. It is the familiar cycle of the second paragraph, not the author's account, that the scene sits badly with.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the live rival, because the scene genuinely does not fit the cycle described in the second paragraph, and a reader who has not yet separated the reported account from the author's takes that misfit for a difficulty.

distractors.why_wrong: The dinner is a particular evening with two people and one rug, which is the opposite of a general claim. The generality arrives afterwards, when the passage moves from this rug to marks whose price is accumulated.
distractors.seductive_element: The scene does end on a wide-sounding sentence about buying the rug and not having the thing, which can be mistaken for the statement of a principle.

vocabulary.passage_use: It does not make the connoisseur a hypocrite
vocabulary.meaning_here: someone whose judgement in a field has been built up by long acquaintance with it
the steady movement of a fashion from one place to the next
built up slowly over time rather than paid for at once

mentor.challenge: One dinner-table exchange and five paragraphs of reflection, ending in a paragraph that refuses to make the accusation you have been preparing. Read the last five sentences slowly.
mentor.one_sentence_summary: The familiar story in which a status marker is copied from below and abandoned from above holds only for markers that can be bought; a marker whose price is hours and company cannot be copied at all, so it is never abandoned, and the test simply moves from owning the object to what one can say about it.
mentor.main_idea: The cycle of imitation and flight assumes that a mark can be acquired by paying for it, and that the copy is then the same mark. That is true of objects. Where the price is accumulated instead, the mark is a relation rather than a thing, the copy is always detectable, and the cycle never starts. Such marks are durable, invisible and untaxable, and to their holders they look like nothing but taste, which the author declines to call insincere.
mentor.simple_explanation:
A guest at dinner says he likes the rug and has been hunting for one like it for two years. The host thanks him, then adds, very lightly, that it is not the kind the guest thinks: different valley, the good workshops there shut long ago, and what is sold under that name now is mostly later copies. Nobody is rude. Nobody scores a point. But something has been settled: the guest could go out and buy the rug and still not have what the host has.

The usual story about status would call this one turn of a wheel. The people at the top pick something up, everyone else copies it, it stops being a marker, so the people at the top drop it and pick up something else. That explains a lot: why holiday spots go in and out of fashion, why names rise and fall, why a word stops being used the moment everyone starts using it.

But look at what that story needs to be true. It needs the marker to be something you can buy, and it needs the bought version to be the same thing. With objects that holds. A coat is a coat, and nobody can tell the copy from the original, so the only defence left to the person at the top is to move on.

Now think about a different kind of marker, one that costs things you cannot hand over: hours, attention, being corrected by people who already know. That marker is not a thing at all. It is a relationship with things, and you cannot post a relationship. So the copy is always spottable, not because the copier is foolish, but because what he is imitating is a history he has not lived. In fact his turning up is what makes the difference visible: nobody corrects you about a rug you never mentioned. So the wheel never turns. Nothing has to be given up, because nothing was really taken. The rug stays where it is. What moves is the test: not do you own one, but what can you say about it.

These markers last much longer and are far harder to see. You cannot tax them, undercut them, or sell them cheaper. And from the inside they do not feel like markers at all. They feel like taste. That is the strongest place a marker can be, because the people who have it can honestly say there is nothing going on.

The author then stops himself. He is not calling the expert a fraud. The pleasure of knowing one valley from another is genuine, and nothing in the argument needs it to be an act. Nor is he saying money no longer buys status. The point is narrower and odder: a marker you had to accumulate does not need abandoning when it spreads, because it does not spread, and a marker nobody can copy has no use for running away.
mentor.why_difficult: The passage invites an accusation and then withdraws it. Everything up to the fifth paragraph reads like an exposure, and the fifth even calls the position the strongest a mark can occupy, which sounds like praise for a tactic. The sixth then says the connoisseur is not a hypocrite and that nothing is being performed, which forces a reader to hold a description of a social mechanism apart from a charge against the people in it. That separation is the hardest thing in the piece, and four of the five questions test it.
mentor.author_intention: To show that the best-known account of how status works has a condition attached to it, and then to describe the case that escapes it without turning the description into an accusation.

paragraph_journey.note: A guest praises a rug; the host corrects him kindly and precisely. Nothing rude happens, and it is established that buying the rug would not get the guest what the host has.
Status marks get copied from below and dropped from above, so the whole system keeps moving. It explains fashions, names and words.
That account needs the mark to be buyable and the copy to be identical. True of objects, where the only defence left is to move on.
Some marks are accumulated, not bought. They are relations, not things, so the copy always shows, and the copier's arrival is what creates the occasion. The cycle never starts; the test simply moves.
Such marks last, cannot be taxed or undercut, leave no receipts, and feel from the inside like nothing but taste, which is the strongest position of all.
This is not a charge of hypocrisy and not a claim that money has stopped working. Only this: a mark that cannot be copied does not need to be abandoned.

mentor.tone_progression: Novelistic and unhurried in the opening scene, then analytic and increasingly dry as the familiar account is examined and its condition exposed, briefly almost admiring in the fifth paragraph, and finally careful, pulling back from the accusation the previous paragraph seemed to be assembling.
key_transitions: 'Notice, though, what that account has to assume.' (opening of paragraph 3): the familiar cycle is given a condition.
'A second kind of mark costs something that cannot be handed over.' (opening of paragraph 4): the case that escapes the cycle arrives.
'The account should not be pressed into saying more than it can carry.' (opening of paragraph 6): the author refuses the accusation his argument has been inviting.
mentor.misunderstanding: Most readers finish believing they have read an exposure of snobbery, in which knowledge is a weapon consciously wielded to keep newcomers out. The passage says nothing of the kind. It describes a property of certain marks, that their price cannot be transferred, and it explicitly declines to describe the people who hold them as performing or scheming. A second misreading keeps the cycle intact and treats these marks as slower-moving cases of it, which the fourth paragraph rules out by saying the cycle does not begin at all.
mentor.traps_summary: The options here hand the author a denunciation he refuses, attach detectability to the wrong kind of mark, invent comparisons of worth and of price, and read an opening scene as an obstacle rather than as an instance. Each is answered from the third and sixth paragraphs, which say what the cycle assumes and what the author is not claiming.
mentor.reading_lesson: Learn to keep a description of a mechanism apart from a judgement of the people inside it, because a passage that describes an advantage will read as an accusation unless you check whether the author ever makes one. Look for the paragraph in which the author states what his claim does not include; in writing about status, class and taste, that paragraph is where the answers live, and readers who are enjoying the exposure tend to skim it.
mentor.real_world: The same distinction sorts out arguments about accents, about which schools their holders describe as unremarkable, and about the difference between owning the equipment for a pursuit and being any good at it.
mentor.takeaway: Some advantages survive being copied, which is why their owners never have to notice that they have them.
mentor.reflection_question: Which of your own preferences would be impossible for someone to adopt this year, and what would give them away if they tried?
